subject.title: [Security] Plaintext credential leakage in diagnostic crash dumps

question: Does a disclosure-safe canary export from current main demonstrate that a credential survives the documented diagnostics sanitization boundary, and should further details move to a private advisory?
rationale: The public report contains no payload or artifact and names mismatched files; confirming the security boundary may require sensitive diagnostic details that should not be requested or investigated through an automated public repair lane.

options.title: Request private canary proof
options.body: Ask for an exact synthetic payload, command, resulting artifact location, and the unredacted canary occurrence through the repository's private security channel before choosing a repair.

options.title: Close as unsupported report
options.body: Close only if a maintainer confirms that the report refers exclusively to documented secret-bearing support bundles rather than the sanitized diagnostics export.

recommendation.title: Request private canary proof
recommendation.body: Ask for an exact synthetic payload, command, resulting artifact location, and the unredacted canary occurrence through the repository's private security channel before choosing a repair.

likelyOwner.reason: The available feature history most directly associates this person with introducing the diagnostics-export surface.
